system_type_reason: Python framework for building LLM application backends (request contract, Action Runtime, TriggerFlow); no end-user agent of its own.

repo_overview.summary: Agently (v4.1.3.7) is a Python framework for building LLM application backends. It gives a unified request contract across model providers, with schema-as-prompt structured output and response parsing. On top of that sit an Action Runtime that executes tools, MCP and sandboxed code and feeds the results back to the model, an AgentTaskLoop / Skills Executor for multi-step goal-driven execution, and TriggerFlow, a signal-driven workflow engine with pause/resume and persistence. Agentic behaviour comes from the framework's built-in loops (action loop, task loop, ReAct skills strategy), which applications wire together.

components.purpose: Agent facade (prompt slots, .output(), .use_actions(), .start()), global Agently entry point, default settings (runtime raise_error, bash timeout 20s, bash aliases)
request lifecycle: ModelRequest builds the prompt and calls the requester, ModelResponse/DataFlow/Result parse and stream, AttemptRunner handles retry attempts
high-level execution: AgentTask/Task.py (goal/success-criteria task loop, effort()), DynamicTask (model-generated DAG), AgentExecution (prompt draft, context, stream, result), SkillsExecutor facade
Action Runtime core: Action, ActionDispatcher, ActionFlowController, normalization/registry/artifacts, ExecutionEnvironment lifecycle, PolicyApproval
TriggerFlow (signal-driven workflow engine: execution, persistence save/load, interrupts pause/resume, recovery diagnostics, sub-flows, processes) and TaskDAG (validation, resolver, runtime executor)
Session (chat history, max_length), Workspace (local backend stores, profiles), Recall
EventCenter, runtime events and context used for observation

swappable plugin implementations: ModelRequester (OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Responses-compatible), ResponseParser (json/xml/yaml/markdown/hybrid), PromptGenerator, ActionRuntime, ActionFlow (TriggerFlow and DAG variants), ActionExecutor (bash/python/node/docker/sqlite/MCP/browse), ExecutionEnvironmentProvider, SkillsExecutor (planner, registry, executor, react/staged and effort strategies), AgentOrchestrator (routing, limits, state, diagnostics), TaskDAGPlanner, ToolManager
Agent mixins: ActionExtension (action loop), ConfigurePrompt, ChatSession/Session, KeyWaiter (early key yield), Workspace, AutoFunc, StreamingPrint
reusable reasoning blocks: Intent, Read, Reason, Act, Observe, Finalize
built-in Browse, Search, Cmd actions and tools
shared helpers: StreamingJSONParser/Completer, DataGuardian, PythonSandbox, MCP client, ModelPool, Settings, Storage
typed data and plugin protocols, settings schemas; FastAPI and ChromaDB adapters

topology.justification: One agent instance carries all roles: route selection (routing.py:130), AgentTask planning, step execution and verification (Task.py:669, 724) and action planning (ActionExtension.py:936) are all requests or executions on the same self.agent with role-specific prompts. DynamicTask/TaskDAG handlers are TriggerFlows or callables (TaskDAGRuntime.py:441-452); the framework defines no second agent type acting autonomously. Multiple agents arise only when user code wires them into handlers, so by the criterion 'Tools != Agents' the system is single-agent.

resilience.name: output-constraint verification with re-request
resilience.what_it_is: After parsing, the response is checked against three constraint layers: required ensure_keys (explicit or auto-derived from $ensure markers in the .output() schema, with presence or not_null policy), strict output via ensure_all_keys (parsed result object must exist), and user-registered validate handlers that may return retryable/stop/raise. On failure the full request is re-issued as a fresh ModelResponse with the same prompt, up to max_retries=3; afterwards a ValueError is raised unless raise_ensure_failure=False. Each retry emits a model.retrying runtime event.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model response and the point where the application or the action loop consumes the structured data (ModelResponseResult.async_get_data). Catches incomplete or semantically invalid structured outputs by re-sampling. Otherwise missing fields or invalid values flow silently into business logic, action dispatch or downstream workflow signals.

resilience.name: automatic output-format degradation to JSON
resilience.what_it_is: When the output format was auto-resolved to a lightweight format (flat_markdown, hybrid, xml_field, yaml_literal) and the parser yields no parsed result, the prompt is switched to output_format=json and the request is re-issued, counted against max_retries and reported as a model.retrying event with retry_reason=format_degradation.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs at data materialization before the constraint checks. Falls back to a more robust output format when a model fails to follow the cheaper format chosen automatically. Otherwise the caller receives empty or None data from an unparseable response.

resilience.name: stream-safe transient provider-error retry
resilience.what_it_is: A provider-agnostic AttemptRunner wraps each model request; plugin handlers classify errors into retry, yield_error or stop. The OpenAICompatible requester retries transport failures only (httpx RequestError, TimeoutError, SSEError; HTTP status errors are passed through), default 2 attempts, configurable or disabled via request_retry. A retry is blocked once output has started streaming (retry_blocked observation). Anthropic and Responses requesters use the same runner with a handler that always yields the error.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the provider call inside ModelResponse, below any agent step. Absorbs network disconnects and timeouts before they surface as a failed step, while the output-started guard keeps a replay from duplicating already streamed tokens to the consumer. Otherwise a transient connection drop fails the request, or a naive replay corrupts the streamed output.

resilience.name: model-call stall detection (first-token, stream-idle and materialization timeouts)
resilience.what_it_is: Layered timeouts that turn a hanging model call into a RuntimeStageStallError with stage-specific diagnostics. Transport level (all three requesters): with the default timeout_mode=first_token the httpx read timeout (default 120s) applies only until the first SSE event, afterwards the stream may run as long as it keeps producing; connect/write/pool are bounded at 30s; an optional stream_idle_timeout bounds the gap between events. Parse level: awaiting the parsed result is bounded by response.materialization_idle_timeout and emits an ERROR event model.response_materialization_stalled. On expiry the stream generator is closed.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the provider transport and at data materialization in ModelResponseResult, below every agent step. Detects providers that never start answering or stall mid-stream and converts the hang into an explicit error that the transient-error retry and key failover can handle, while long healthy streams are left running. Otherwise the calling agent step or workflow blocks indefinitely on a dead connection.

resilience.name: API-key pool failover
resilience.what_it_is: Model profiles can reference an api_key_pools entry with a selection strategy (fixed, random, round_robin, least_used) and a failover policy. On a provider error with a retryable status (default 401, 403, 429) or a timeout, the policy or a user handler picks try_next, retry_same, a specific key or raise; the new key is written into the request-local settings, auth headers are rebuilt and the request is re-sent. Attempts are capped at the number of keys by default, and failover is blocked once output has streamed unless allow_stream_retry_after_output is set. Implemented identically in all three model requesters.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the provider HTTP transport, below the AttemptRunner. Handles rate-limit, quota and revoked-key failures that the transient-error retry deliberately passes through. Otherwise a single exhausted or blocked key fails the request although working keys remain in the pool.

resilience.name: lenient JSON extraction and repair
resilience.what_it_is: Deterministic recovery chain in the JSON response parser: all JSON blocks are located in the free-text response and, if several exist, the one with the best match score against the .output() schema is chosen; truncated brackets, strings and comments are auto-closed (StreamingJSONCompleter); the result is parsed leniently with json5; on failure structural characters are repaired (full-width punctuation, typographic quotes) and parsing is retried, flagging repaired=true; the parsed data is optionally validated into a Pydantic result object.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in the ResponseParser right after the model response and before the output-constraint verification with re-request. Recovers typical model formatting faults (surrounding prose or code fences, truncation, non-ASCII punctuation) locally in the parser, saving a model call. Otherwise each of these faults yields None data or triggers a costly re-request.

resilience.name: schema-as-prompt output contract
resilience.what_it_is: The .output() schema is rendered by the PromptGenerator into an OUTPUT REQUIREMENT prompt section with the data format, the field structure and, under ensure_all_keys, a strict-structure guarantee stating that all fields are required and extra fields are disallowed. Fields carrying an $ensure marker are rendered as required.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at prompt construction before every structured model call. Steers the model toward output that the parser and the constraint checks can accept on the first attempt, which reduces repair work and re-requests. Its effect depends on model compliance; the code-level enforcement of the same contract lives in the lenient JSON repair and the output-constraint verification.

resilience.name: human approval gate for side-effecting actions
resilience.what_it_is: Actions whose spec sets approval_required, or whose merged policy has approval_mode='always', are routed through policy_approval.async_resolve before the executor runs. The default handler input_timeout_fail asks for [y/N] on the console and denies after input_timeout_seconds (default 30); in a non-interactive environment it denies immediately (fail closed). The same gate guards provisioning of execution environments (approval_mode='never' denies outright). TriggerFlowActionFlow persists the pending approval key and decisions in flow state so an interrupted run resumes at the gated action. In TaskDAG graphs, a fail_closed approval policy requires an approval requirement on every task that declares side effects and rejects the graph otherwise, and approval tasks pause the graph through the same policy_approval gate.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the planned action and executor.execute() inside ActionDispatcher. Stops the model from triggering side effects (exec, write, resource allocation) unsupervised; a denial returns an approval_required or blocked result that the next planning round sees. Otherwise a wrong or harmful plan executes immediately against the host.

resilience.name: allowlist-restricted sandbox executors and workspace path confinement
resilience.what_it_is: Shell actions (Cmd) run only if the command matches an allowlisted prefix (default ls, rg, cat, pwd, whoami, date, head, tail) and the workdir resolves under allowed roots; violations return need_approval, which the dispatcher maps to an approval_required result. The subprocess has a 20 s timeout. The model-visible kwarg allow_unsafe lets the model bypass the command allowlist itself. Python actions run via exec with a whitelisted __builtins__ set (no __import__), a return-type whitelist and blocked access to underscore attributes. The dispatcher blocks any action with sandbox_required whose executor is unsandboxed. Workspace file actions resolve every path against the workspace root and reject paths outside it; reads are capped at max_file_bytes=20000, write access is disabled by default, and an isolated temp directory can serve as root.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the executor layer at the point where model-generated code or commands hit the host. Contains the blast radius of wrong or injected commands to read-mostly tools in a bounded directory. Otherwise any model output runs with full user privileges.

def resolve_workspace_path(path: str | Path = "."):
    candidate = Path(path)
    if not candidate.is_absolute():
        candidate = root_path / candidate
    resolved = candidate.expanduser().resolve()
    try:
        resolved.relative_to(root_path)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise ValueError(f"Path is outside workspace root: { path }") from error
    return resolved

resilience.name: per-action execution budget (timeout and output byte cap)
resilience.what_it_is: policy.timeout_seconds wraps executor.execute in asyncio.wait_for; on timeout the dispatcher releases action-scoped environment handles and returns an error result. policy.max_output_bytes truncates the JSON-serialized action output to the byte limit and sets meta.truncated. Both policy values have no default, so this policy budget is opt_in. Separately, the built-in workspace read_file action caps every read at max_file_bytes=20000 by default and reports truncated in its result; this tool-level cap is active whenever the workspace tools are mounted.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the single action execution inside ActionDispatcher.async_execute. Converts a hanging tool into an error observation for the next planning round and caps how much tool output enters the context. Otherwise one stuck tool blocks the whole action loop and one oversized output floods the prompt.

resilience.name: action-result digest with artifact offloading and recall
resilience.what_it_is: Results of instruction-heavy executors (bash, python, nodejs, docker, sqlite, browse, search) are stored in full as artifacts; the model sees a digest with compacted previews (strings cut at 4000/8000 chars, max 40 items, depth 2) and artifact refs. A read_action_artifact action is injected into the action list so the model can fetch the full value on demand. Keys matching api_key, token, password, secret, authorization etc. are replaced by [REDACTED] in stored artifacts and previews.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between action execution and the next planning prompt (done_plans / last_round_records are converted to model-visible records in every ActionFlow round). Keeps per-round context growth bounded while the full data stays retrievable, and keeps credentials out of the prompt. Otherwise raw tool dumps accumulate across rounds and exhaust the context window.

resilience.name: action-loop round cap and wall-clock timeout

resilience.name: verifier-gated plan/execute/verify iteration loop
resilience.what_it_is: Each AgentTask iteration builds a context pack, asks the model to plan one bounded step, runs the step as an agent execution that must return evidence, then issues a separate verifier request against every success criterion. The verifier prompt counts numeric criteria exactly, demands source evidence and forbids completion when any required action or validation command failed. is_complete ends the task as accepted, requires_block ends it as blocked, otherwise the replan_instruction drives the next iteration; after max_iterations (default 3) the task ends with accepted=False and artifact_status 'partial'.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the whole agent execution as an outer task loop with a critic step between execution and acceptance. Catches steps that claim completion on insufficient evidence and turns the gap into a concrete replan. Otherwise an incomplete or hallucinated result is returned as the final task result.

resilience.name: per-execution model-request budget
resilience.what_it_is: Before every model request ModelResponse calls consume_model_request on the current AgentExecution context; once max_model_requests is reached it records a limit_exceeded event and raises AgentExecutionLimitExceeded before the request is sent. AgentTask passes limits={'max_model_requests': 3} by default to each step execution; plain agent executions have no limit unless configured. Effort presets (e.g. effort='medium') can set max_model_requests, max_seconds and max_no_progress_seconds as one bundle when effort is configured.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the single chokepoint for all model calls inside an execution, including the inner action loop and output re-requests. Caps the cost of one execution step. Otherwise nested retries and planning rounds multiply model calls unboundedly.

evidence.snippet:
def consume_model_request(self, *, response_id: str | None = None, run_id: str | None = None):
    limit = self.limits.get("max_model_requests")
    if limit is not None and self.model_request_count >= int(limit):
        event = {
            "type": "limit_exceeded",
            "limit_name": "max_model_requests",
            "limit_value": limit,
            "used": self.model_request_count,
            "response_id": response_id,
            "run_id": run_id,
        }
        self.limit_events.append(event)
        raise AgentExecutionLimitExceeded(
            (
                "AgentExecution model request budget exceeded: "
                f"max_model_requests={ limit }, used={ self.model_request_count }."
            ),
            limit_name="max_model_requests",
            limit_value=limit,
            used=self.model_request_count,
        )
    self.model_request_count += 1
self.limits = dict(limits or {"max_model_requests": 3})

resilience.name: hard deadline and no-progress watchdog
resilience.what_it_is: ActionRuntime stages run under a sliding idle deadline: the deadline is recomputed from context.last_progress_at, which every progress event refreshes, and only when no progress arrived for stage_idle_timeout or limits.max_no_progress_seconds is the stage task cancelled and RuntimeStageStallError raised with the last progress event. AgentTask wraps each plan, execute and verify request in asyncio.wait_for with request_timeout_seconds, falling back to max_no_progress_seconds or max_seconds. All values are unset by default. At the orchestrator level await_route_with_limits wraps the whole route execution with a hard deadline (max_seconds from execution start) and the sliding idle deadline (max_no_progress_seconds), waits until the nearer one, then cancels the route and raises RuntimeStageStallError with status 'timed_out' or 'stalled'.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the long-running phases of an agent execution (action planning and execution stages, task-level model requests). Distinguishes slow but active work from a hung stage and aborts only the latter with a diagnosable error. Otherwise a stalled stage blocks the task indefinitely with no signal to the caller.

resilience.name: required-action evidence gate
resilience.what_it_is: After the model_request route finishes, the action logs are checked against the action ids declared via require_actions; every required action must appear with status success or partial_success. Missing or failed required actions end the execution as 'blocked' with accepted=False and a reason listing the missing and failed actions.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at route completion, between the agent's answer and its acceptance as the execution result. Deterministically checks that the mandated tools actually ran and succeeded. Otherwise the model answers from its own knowledge while the caller assumes a tool-backed result.

resilience.name: durable execution snapshot with validated reload
resilience.what_it_is: execution.save() serializes interrupts, runtime and flow data, result, lease state and a resume ledger into a snapshot (optionally only when idle via require_idle). async_save() writes it to a snapshot store with an optional compare-and-swap on expected_state_version. load() checks the snapshot contract and, with validate_resources=True, refuses to restore when required runtime resources are missing. On inspection the resume ledger is diagnosed for requests that were accepted or dispatched but never completed.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the boundary of a TriggerFlow execution, the runtime that hosts action loops and TaskDAG graphs. Lets a paused or crashed execution continue in a new process from its last saved state, and the CAS write stops two workers from overwriting each other's progress. Otherwise a process restart loses all intermediate work of a long workflow and half-finished resumes stay invisible.

resilience.name: idempotent interrupt resume with self-resume cap and lease fencing
resilience.what_it_is: continue_with() deduplicates resumes by resume_request_id: a repeated request with the same value returns the existing interrupt, a conflicting value raises. Interrupts that resume to themselves are capped by max_resumes (default 1) and exceeding the cap emits triggerflow.self_resume_limit_reached and raises. When an owner lease (claim_lease/heartbeat_lease with lease_ttl) has expired, the resume is rejected with a triggerflow.lease.expired event.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the resume entry point of paused executions (human approval, external waits). Blocks duplicate side effects from client retries, stops pause/resume cycles from looping forever and fences out a worker whose lease ran out. Otherwise a retried webhook runs a step twice, a self-resuming node loops indefinitely and two workers continue the same execution concurrently.

resilience.name: per-task failure isolation with skip fallback
resilience.what_it_is: When a TaskDAG task raises, the error type and message are stored in task_failures, the task status is set to failed and a failed:<task_id> event is emitted. resilience.name: structural plan validation with re-plan
resilience.what_it_is: The TaskDAG planner registers validate_output as validate handler on the planning request. It runs validate_task_dag on the model's graph (duplicate ids, missing dependencies, dependency cycles via topological sort, executor resolver entries, semantic output refs, side-effect approval policy, schema version) and returns ok=False with a reason on failure. The generic output-constraint retry then re-requests the plan, up to max_retries=3.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the planner model call and graph execution in DynamicTask. Rejects plans that cannot execute before any task runs and makes the model produce a new one. Otherwise a cyclic or unresolvable graph fails at execution time after partial work.

resilience.name: session context-window trimming with pluggable resize strategy
resilience.what_it_is: A Session keeps the full_context and a separate context_window that is injected as chat_history into each request. After every history change, with auto_resize=True (hard-set by SessionExtension), an analysis handler measures the window in serialized characters and selects the simple_cut strategy once it exceeds session.max_length. simple_cut keeps the most recent messages that fit the limit and, when even the last message is too long, keeps only its last max_length characters. Custom analysis and resize handlers can be registered, and a memo they return is injected into the prompt as CHAT SESSION MEMO.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the multi-turn chat history and prompt assembly of every agent request with an active session. Bounds the prompt size of long conversations while the full history stays available for custom strategies. Otherwise the growing chat history eventually overflows the model context window or inflates the cost of every turn.

resilience.name: budgeted recall context pack
resilience.what_it_is: Workspace.build_context runs a recall profile (plan, retrieve, build) over workspace records and packs them into a character budget: AgentTask passes {'chars': 6000} by default, the builder falls back to 12000 chars or tokens*4. Keeps the recalled evidence within a fixed size as the task workspace grows and keeps the loop running when recall fails. Otherwise every iteration's prompt grows with the whole task history and a recall error aborts the task.

resilience.name: default-off skill capability mounting with approval
resilience.what_it_is: Every capability_need declared by a selected Skill is resolved against skills.capability_policy. The default mode is 'off', which blocks the need. Mode 'approval' asks policy_approval and blocks unless the decision is approved. Mode 'allow' mounts the capability, and a mount error also blocks. Any blocked or unapproved need stops the Skill execution before an effort strategy runs and returns status 'blocked' with diagnostics.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between Skill planning and Skill execution in the skills route. Restricts which tools and resources a Skill can attach to the agent to those explicitly granted by the operator. Otherwise an installed Skill silently extends the agent with arbitrary capabilities such as bash or network access.

resilience.name: budgeted skill context injection

def _collect_prompt_guidance(self, contract: SkillContract, *, max_chars: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    guidance = _ensure_dict(contract.get("guidance"))
    content = str(guidance.get("content") or "")
    if not content.strip():
        return []
    trimmed = content[:max_chars]
    return [{
        "skill_id": str(contract.get("skill_id", "")),
        "path": str(guidance.get("path") or "SKILL.md"),
        "title": str(contract.get("card", {}).get("display_name", "")),
        "content": trimmed,
        "truncated": len(content) > len(trimmed),
    }]
